title: More DWUGs: Extending and Evaluating Word Usage Graph Datasets in Multiple Languages

selection.evidence: Opened 2026-11-26 night to test arena-lsc F37 (task-size change gold is mostly sampling noise) against an independent human replication: the paper's DWUG 'resampled' sets annotate 15 words per language with 25 new usages per period, the SemEval-2027 Task 3 sample size. Chosen because it ships the data (Zenodo), before reading its results.

cost.compute_notes: PDF text via pdftotext, read in full (main text, Tables 2-5, Appendices A-C); figures 3, 5-7 not read as images. Zip downloads: DWUG EN/DE/SV V3 and resampled already on disk for arena-lsc; V1/V2 fetched three times (~140 MB each time) because two extractions failed, keeping only the stats CSVs (fetch_versions.py). All analyses CPU, under 1 min each.

triggers: do graded semantic change scores replicate when usages are resampled
how reliable is DWUG change gold at 25 usages per period
word usage graph annotation density versus number of usages
Jensen-Shannon distance sense distribution sampling noise

claims.statement: Sense distributions of the resampled data (15 words per language, 25 new uses per period, densely annotated) are close to those of DWUG V1/V2: mean JS distance 0.08-0.22, maximum 0.48, some words at 0; hence the costly SemEval annotation can be approximated with a simpler, cheaper procedure.
claims.scope: Section 6.3, Table 4 (columns read as min / mean / max). 'Trimming the longer distribution to match the shorter one'; which distribution (pooled or per period) is not stated.

our_assessment.why: Approximately reproduced from the deposited stats with per-period trimmed distributions (DE .11/.09, EN .18/.17, SV .19/.16 vs printed .10/.08, .22/.19, .19/.10; SV V2 and EN V1 min differ). But the distance compares frequency-SORTED profiles, not senses: every zero comes from a side with a single cluster (6/15 DE, 2/15 EN, 3-4/15 SV), and pairing each resampled word with a DIFFERENT word gives 0.13 DE, 0.19-0.20 EN, 0.21-0.23 SV (pooled variant; same-word 0.07, 0.13, 0.18-0.22). For SV the same-word distance is not below the different-word control, so Table 4 cannot show that the same senses were recovered there; for DE and EN it shows similar sense-frequency profiles, not matched senses.

claims.statement: Change scores of the densely annotated resampled graphs are robust to added random edges: Spearman with the unperturbed scores stays 0.81-1.00 (DE, SV) and 0.61-0.80 (EN) at 40% noisy edges, vs 0.21-0.60 for V1-V3.
claims.scope: Appendix B, Figure 5 (figure not read as an image; numbers from the appendix text).

our_assessment.why: Would need the WUG clustering pipeline rerun on perturbed graphs; not done. Note it measures robustness to annotation noise within one usage sample, not replication across usage samples (c4).

claims.statement: Graded change scores replicate only partly across independent usage samples: Spearman of change_graded between DWUG V3 (~100 uses per period) and the resampled sets (25 per period, new annotators) is 0.79 EN [0.41, 0.93], 0.80 DE [0.36, 0.94], 0.65 SV [0.09, 0.95], pooled 45 words 0.76. Usage sampling alone (V3 period distributions taken as truth, both a V3-sized and a 25+25 multinomial replicate drawn) predicts 0.82 [0.61, 0.94], 0.93 [0.86, 0.98], 0.90 [0.77, 0.97]; observed DE and SV fall at the 0th percentile, EN at the 36th. SV resampled scores are higher on average by +0.16 (0.44 vs 0.28; usage sampling predicts +0.01), e.g. antyda 0.25 -> 0.88, konduktör 0.27 -> 0.78.
claims.scope: 15 words per language, two periods, between-word ranking only. The simulation treats V3's clusters (many singletons: K up to 33) as true senses, so it is a lower bound on usage-sampling noise only in the sense of being computed from the estimated distributions. The SV resample was annotated twice after low agreement (paper Sec. 5.3) and resampled K is much smaller than V3 K throughout, so annotation design and clustering differ along with the usages.

our_assessment.why: Own measurement from the deposits; holds for these 45 words and the deposited opt clusterings. Reading: at 25 uses per period, pure usage sampling would still let graded change replicate at ~0.82-0.93 between words; the observed shortfall in DE and SV is the graph (annotators, edge sampling, clustering), not the usage sample.

relations.why: Adds annotation rounds 5-6 (V2, V3) and an independent resample to the DWUG datasets recorded there.
Independent support for goworek c3 / arena-lsc F37: the change gold depends on sense structure and annotation as much as on change; here graded change replicates at .65-.80 across usage samples.

open_questions: Does the SemEval-2027 Task 3 gold (about 20 uses per period, several periods) replicate across independent usage samples? This paper's resample is the only human replication I know of, and it has two periods and 15 words per language.

Is the SV shift (+0.16) from the new annotators, the random edge sampling, or the clustering? Separable only by reclustering the resampled graphs with the V3 pipeline parameters, or by using the judgments directly.
c2 (robustness to noisy edges) not checked: rerun the WUG pipeline on perturbed resampled graphs.
